messages.subject: Error - time varying covariates
parts:
Hi All,

This is my first post on this list, and I'm definitely not a secr expert, so please forgive any posting errors on my part.

My question is about an error when trying model model average secr models that include a time-varying covariate. I'm working on a study investigating effects of feral hog abundance on white-tailed deer density. We're running a set of 5 models, with 2 of the 5 including a time-varying covariate called "hog" (see R code below). The time-varying covariate seems to be throwing a wrench in the 2 models below, and I can't figure out why. 

three <- secr.fit(input.data, mask = NULL, model = list(D ~ session, g0 ~ t + session + hog, sigma ~ session + t), 
                  start = start.mod, trace = T, ncores = 4, buffer = 2000)
four <- secr.fit(input.data, mask = NULL, model = list(D ~ 1, g0 ~ t + session + hog, sigma ~ session + t), 
                 start = start.mod, trace = T, ncores = 4, buffer = 2000, verify=T)

I get the following error when calling models three and four:
three
Error in secr.lpredictor(formula = models[[x]], newdata = newdata, indx = parindices[[x]],  : 
  model covariate hog not found in 'newdata'
four
Error in secr.lpredictor(formula = models[[x]], newdata = newdata, indx = parindices[[x]],  : 
  model covariate hog not found in 'newdata'

Similarly, when I try to model average the set of 5 models, I get the following error:
> mod.list <- secrlist(null, one, two, three, four) #note models null, one, and two run fine and don't have the hog covariate
> mod.avg <- model.average(mod.list)
Error in secr.lpredictor(formula = object1$model[[x]], newdata = newdata,  : 
  model covariate hog not found in 'newdata'

If I remove models three and four from the "mod.list" object, there is no error, which leads me to believe there's something going wrong with the hog covariate. The hog covariate shows up in the input.data (data snip below), so I'm not sure what's causing the error. I'm wondering if there's a problem with the syntax for models three and four? Maybe I'm not specifying the time-varying covariate correctly. (I've also tried running models three and four above, specifying "timecov=input.data$hog", but still get the same error.)

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Error - time varying covariates
parts:
Hi James
Without delving too deeply into your example - I suspect your models fitted just fine and the problem comes in 'predicting' real parameter estimates. For example, AIC(three, four) should be OK?

For time-varying trap covariates you must use the 'newdata' argument of predict() to specify the levels for which you want estimates. Thus predict(three, newdata=data.frame(hog = ...). This is shown in the Examples of the ?timevarying help. Not sure where it is documented otherwise. (I'm sceptical in general about fully time-specific (t) models, and there may be difficulty if trap covariates are also time-varying).
Murray

messages.author: 23dd9a16424deeb8
messages.subject: Re: Error - time varying covariates
parts: Yes, AIC(three, four) is OK, as is AIC(null, one, two, three, four). Specifying 'newdata' worked like a charm - that error isn't thrown anymore. Thanks again and I appreciate the prompt response!
